stem:
Wasim chooses the unit $\dfrac{1}{5}$ metre and finds that a ribbon is covered by exactly $7$ such units.

Which claim measures the ribbon correctly?

options.text: Report the length as $\dfrac{7}{5}$ metre even if the unit length changes mid-count, without keeping one fixed metre as the whole.
Say that writing $\dfrac{7}{5}$ metre is what creates the seven copies of $\dfrac{1}{5}$ metre.
Count $7$ copies of the unit $\dfrac{1}{5}$ metre, so the ribbon length is $\dfrac{7}{5}$ metre.
Also treat the same $7$ copies as settling the ribbon's area in square metres, beyond this length count.

teacher.key_rationale: A length counted in fractional units is $n$ copies of $1/d$: here $7$ copies of $1/5$ metre give $7/5$ metre. Dropping a fixed whole, reversing the write-up and the count, or stretching the count into area all leave this hinge.
